tag_type: HA (YPYDVPDYA) with PGG linkers each side
paper_quote: was inserted in the extracellular P2-M4 loop of human TASK-Δi20 at amino acid position 214
paper_numbering_basis: full-length human TASK-1 (KCNK3, NM_002246) numbering, inferred: UniProt P2-M4 extracellular loop is 205-222 and 214 lies inside it; if Δi20 removed 20 residues upstream, position 214 of the deleted protein would be 234 (inside M4), contradicting the stated loop; the construct was built on the Δi20 variant, whose deletion is not defined in the accessible text (ref 13, Rinné 2015 JMCC, PMID 25655935, is paywalled)
notes: Original row named KCNK5/TASK-2 (wrong gene). Surface = chemiluminescence ELISA on intact (non-permeabilized) Xenopus oocytes with rat anti-HA (Fig 2c, WT-HA, and all alanine mutants on the WT-HA background); anti-HA westerns on oocyte lysates (Fig 3). TEVC currents (Fig 2b) are reported for wild-type and mutant TASK-1 without stating that the HA construct was recorded, so function of the tagged channel is not explicitly shown. All mutant alanine positions (L48-L62 etc.) are quoted in full-length numbering consistent with UniProt (L48, Y52, N53, L54, S55, Y59, L62 all match O14649), supporting full-length numbering for 214 as well.

notes: Already in the gold standard from this paper; listed to verify the arithmetic. tag_type: GFP / super-ecliptic pHluorin N-terminal fusion with artificial signal sequence (per abstract); HA not mentioned
paper_quote: An artificial signal sequence (SS) was required for efficient surface expression of CB1 receptor chimeras, which behaved like wild-type CB1 receptors in functional assays.
paper_numbering_basis: not determinable: the residues-25/26 junction is only a second-hand statement in PMID 33097803 (ref 27 there is McDonald 2007); McDonald 2007 full text is subscription-only (Elsevier, 403; no PMC, no repository copy found) and its abstract names GFP/SEP fusions, not HA
notes: Original row quote is from the GLuc paper PMID 33097803 (PMC7584592): in some other cases the fusion of such chimeric proteins has been done between residues 25 and 26 of the extracellular N terminus ... 27, where 27 = McDonald NA, Henstridge CM, Connolly CN, Irving AJ, Mol Cell Neurosci 2007;35:237-248 (the bioRxiv 10.1101/2024.03.21.586146 v1 text contains no 25/26 statement and its ref 27 is Novy et al. 2022). Human CNR1 S25|N26 recorded for reference only; exact junction, tag, species and the surface/functional evidence of the primary paper could not be verified without the paywalled full text, so no positive is recoverable from accessible sources. The abstract reports surface expression in live COS7/HEK293 cells and neurons and wild-type-like function for the SS-GFP/SEP chimeras, but gives no residue numbers.

paper_quote: polyserase-3 is a secreted protein such as polyserase-2, but lacks additional domains like the type II transmembrane motif
notes: The FLAG construct is polyserase-3 = PRSS53 (UniProt Q2L4Q9, 553 aa, signal peptide 1-23, no transmembrane segment, UniProt subcellular location Secreted citing this PMID; EMBL AJ627035). The paper shows anti-FLAG signal only after Triton permeabilization, no cell-surface immunostaining, and the protein in conditioned medium (Fig 4). Polyserase-3 is not a membrane protein, so no surface-protein tag site can be recovered; TMPRSS9/polyserase-1 was never tagged in this paper.
